title: Find the Lexicographically Largest String From the Box II
summary: Given a string word and an integer numFriends, Alice organizes a game for her numFriends friends with multiple rounds.
statement: Given a string word and an integer numFriends, Alice organizes a game for her numFriends friends with multiple rounds. In each round, word is split into numFriends non-empty strings uniquely. All split words are placed in a box. Determine the lexicographically largest string from the box after all rounds. Lexicographical order compares strings by their first differing character, or by their lengths if the first min(a.length, b.length) characters are the same.
constraints: word has 1–200,000 lowercase letters and 1 <= num_friends <= len(word).
Consider every split into num_friends nonempty consecutive parts.
Return the lexicographically largest part appearing across all splits.
hints: The answer starts at the lexicographically greatest suffix but cannot exceed n-numFriends+1 characters.
Find the greatest suffix in linear time by eliminating losing starts with two pointers.
Compare candidate suffixes at their first mismatch, skip the losing matched block, then truncate the winner.
Every skipped start shares the compared prefix and loses at the mismatch, so it cannot be the maximal suffix.
editorial: Every skipped start shares the compared prefix and loses at the mismatch, so it cannot be the maximal suffix.

tests.explanation: The part dbc can appear while leaving a for the other friend, and it is lexicographically largest.
With one friend, the full word is the only part.
